title: Finite Q3 state-dependent GNS Gram polar transport
question: For the same finite Q3 OS word block on nested path volumes, does a state-dependent Gram polar transport give an exact finite GNS metric congruence, and which compatibility conditions remain unproved for a thermodynamic common carrier?
method: Compile verification/lean/Tect/R342.lean with the pinned lake toolchain and require a zero exit status with the gram_transport_congruence declaration registered at its LF-normalized SHA-256.
Rebuild the d=3 Q3 Hamiltonians independently on path2, path3 and path4 with chi=1, r=-1, g=3/5, c=3/5 and lambda=1/10, using shifted finite spectra for the Euclidean transfer words.

For path2->path3 and path3->path4 compare source-0 q, p, qp and pq positive-half transfer-word blocks at beta=0.25,0.5 and tau fractions 0.125,0.25. Form each volume's normalized finite Gram matrix, positive square root and state-dependent map M=R_large^-1 R_small.
Check positive support, the finite congruence M^* G_large M=G_small, relative Gram changes, transport distance, condition numbers, and the dependence of a q,p subblock on the full q,p,qp,pq block.
Run a non-importing independent reconstruction and an integrated verifier that compares all rows, scope flags, Lean R342, registry integrity and the finite-only QFT scope firewall.
finding: R342 compiles and the primary lane passes 29/29 assertions on four nested word blocks; the independent lane passes 28/28 and the integrated lane passes 13/13 with Lean PASS. Every declared Gram block has positive support above 1e-10. The state-dependent polar map gives a maximum relative congruence residual of 3.264003583537878e-13 in the primary lane and 4.89663115986951e-13 independently, with maximum relative Gram change 9.057857978223803e-05 and maximum transport distance 0.047556166181807864. The q,p subblock differs materially from the full-block restriction (maximum dependence 4.352447611324977; subblock residual up to 5.881899365965393e-05), while all four full blocks remain finite positive and congruent.
decision_reason: The finite data support an exact state-dependent metric transport for each declared nested word block, but the transport depends on the volume, beta and selected word block and is not an algebra/action embedding. The positive subblock dependence and large condition numbers show why this cannot be promoted to a canonical common carrier without compatibility and uniformity estimates. It is a route-local finite advance, not a thermodynamic obstruction theorem or QFT closure.

adversarial_review.check: Each finite Gram block is checked for positive eigenvalues above the declared support floor before inverse square roots are formed; singular-limit directions would require a separate support reduction.
M=R_large^-1 R_small is tested through M^*G_large M=G_small; the map is not confused with an operator embedding from the smaller tensor algebra.
The block contains q, p, qp and pq at two finite times only; arbitrary products, adjoints, rational translates and the full local algebra are not silently included.
The Gram matrices use each volume's own finite Gibbs partition function; the polar map is allowed to depend on beta, volume and the selected word block.
Condition numbers and minimum eigenvalues are recorded; numerical congruence residuals are compared with an explicit tolerance and are not called exact QFT equalities.
The q,p subblock is compared with the restriction of the full q,p,qp,pq transport and its nonzero residual is retained as a compatibility diagnostic rather than hidden.
The independent lane rebuilds the Q3 Hamiltonian, transfer words, Gram blocks and polar factors without importing the primary program.
R342 certifies only the finite matrix congruence identity under invertibility; spectral values and thermodynamic statements remain Python evidence/open analysis.

Finite support-aware Gram transport does not prove action intertwining, spatial net compatibility, all-shape Cauchy, common alpha, Hamiltonian-OS identification, a gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.

qft_interface.closed: For the declared finite nested Q3 word blocks, positive Gram support and a state-dependent polar congruence are explicitly computed and independently reproduced.
qft_interface.open: Compatibility under word enlargement and time translates, product/star/action intertwining, a spatial inductive net, source/volume/cutoff/beta-uniform Cauchy, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, GNS gap and continuum remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 finite evidence only; no heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, physical-empty reference, Sector-A closure or Pre-A closure is supplied.

next_action: Test transport compatibility under one additional ordered product and a time translate across the nested pair; if residuals depend on the chosen block or beta, keep the state-dependent map as finite-only and derive the missing uniform action-intertwining estimate.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite nested Q3 GNS Gram-polar checkpoint. It is not a thermodynamic common-Hilbert theorem, a common-alpha construction, a mass-gap proof, a continuum result, or a QFT/Clay closure.
no_overclaim: This record promotes only the finite positive Gram support and support-aware polar metric congruence for the declared word blocks. It does not prove or refute another common OS carrier, action-compatible spatial transport, direct Cauchy convergence, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, a GNS gap, continuum removal, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or a Clay result.
